profile.summary: LOL-EVE (Language Of Life for Evolutionary Variant Effects) scores the effect of insertions and deletions (indels) in human gene promoters without task-specific training. It is a conditional autoregressive transformer trained on 13.6 million mammalian promoter sequences, each tagged with its gene, species and clade. A variant is scored by comparing how likely the model finds the reference and the variant promoter sequence.

summary_quotes.text: We present LOL-EVE (Language Of Life for Evolutionary Variant Effects), a conditional autoregressive transformer trained on 13.6 million mammalian promoter sequences.
LOL-EVE enables zero-shot prediction of indel effects in human promoters.
**Control code integration**: Incorporates gene, species, and clade information

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LOL-EVE is a causal language model based on the CTRL architecture, with 12 transformer layers, hidden size 768 and 12 attention heads; the paper gives a feed-forward dimension of 8192. Each input starts with control codes for the gene, species and clade, followed by the promoter DNA between [SOS] and [EOS] tokens, one token per base so that indels do not shift the tokenisation; training sequences were up to 1000 base pairs. In the paper, the gene is represented by the mean-pooled ESM2 (650M) embedding of its canonical human protein, kept frozen and projected to the model width, which the authors say lets the model handle genes not seen in training; species and clade have learned embeddings. Position embeddings are absolute for the control codes and restart at the start of the DNA sequence. During training the control codes are dropped at random. To score a variant, the reference and variant sequences are each run through the model with the same control codes, the summed cross-entropy of each is computed, and the score is the variant's minus the reference's, with higher meaning more deleterious.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is published, Marks-lab/LOL-EVE on Hugging Face; this page read revision 397bbb87. Its custom model code describes itself as a simplified wrapper that builds a standard CTRL language model with the configured sizes, and its comments say that in practice this would load the actual trained model. The wrapper does not refer to ESM embeddings or adaptive position embeddings. The repository's example_usage.py uses the same wrapper and only prints the shape of the output logits. The repository's own scoring script takes a local checkpoint, tokeniser, genome and embedding file instead. A result should state which route was used (the Hugging Face wrapper or the repository script), the Hugging Face revision, and the control codes given. The paper is the MLCB 2025 work; the model card links a bioRxiv preprint and says the link is to be updated.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Conditional autoregressive (causal) genomic language model for zero-shot promoter variant effect prediction.

quotes.text: a conditional autoregressive transformer trained on 13.6 million mammalian promoter sequences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: CTRL-based transformer: 12 layers, hidden size 768, 12 attention heads, feed-forward dimension 8192 (from the paper), vocabulary of 39,378 tokens, adaptive local position embeddings, with gene, species and clade control codes. In the paper the gene code is a frozen ESM2 protein embedding projected to the model width.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Text of the form 'gene species clade [SOS] sequence [EOS]', for example 'brca1 human primate [SOS] ... [EOS]', where the sequence is promoter DNA (A, T, G, C). Variant scoring takes paired reference and variant sequences.
facts.source_locator: README: Input Format; Using Hugging Face Model

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Next-token logits. The documented variant score is the summed cross-entropy of the variant sequence minus that of the reference; higher means more deleterious.

quotes.text: # Score is the difference (higher = more deleterious)

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 235 million, as the paper states for the model it describes. This figure has not been checked against the published pytorch_model.bin weights, and the Hugging Face model code is a simplified wrapper around a standard CTRL model, so the files read do not confirm that the published checkpoint has this count. The README and card give no count, and the weights are a pytorch_model.bin file, so Hugging Face gives no safetensors count.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: PromoterZoo: 13.6 million sequences, including reverse complements, from 447 mammalian species in the Zoonomia project. For each of 19,254 human protein-coding genes (NCBI RefSeq, GRCh38.p14, annotation release 109) the first exon was lifted over to each species and the 1,000 base pairs upstream taken as the promoter. Human chromosome 19 genes, with their orthologues, were held out for validation. Each sequence carries gene, species and clade information. The data is published as the PromoterZoo dataset on Hugging Face.

strengths.text: Aimed at indels in promoters, a variant class the developers say current methods handle poorly, and scores them zero-shot from sequence likelihood.

quotes.text: current methods struggle to predict effects of insertions and deletions (indels) that can disrupt gene expression
LOL-EVE enables zero-shot prediction of indel effects in human promoters.

strengths.text: Conditions on gene, species and clade through control codes, so the same sequence can be scored in its gene and species context.
Released with three promoter indel benchmark datasets (ultra-rare variants, causal eQTLs, TFBS disruption) and the PromoterZoo training data on Hugging Face.

quotes.text: We introduce three new benchmarks for promoter indel prediction: ultra rare variant prioritization, causal eQTL identification, and transcription factor binding site disruption analysis.

limitations.text: The Hugging Face model code calls itself a simplified demonstration wrapper around a standard CTRL model and does not use the ESM gene embeddings or adaptive position embeddings the README describes, so results from it may not match the paper's model.

run_guide.summary: Install the Python requirements, load LOL-EVE from Hugging Face and score two example sequence pairs with the README's log-likelihood difference.

Network access to Hugging Face; the model loads with trust_remote_code=True.

steps.title: Score example variants
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch
import pandas as pd

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Marks-lab/LOL-EVE')
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('Marks-lab/LOL-EVE', trust_remote_code=True)

def score_variants_hf(variants_df, gene, species, clade):
    scores = []
    for _, row in variants_df.iterrows():
        ref_seq = f"{gene} {species} {clade} [SOS] {row['sequence']} [EOS]"
        var_seq = f"{gene} {species} {clade} [SOS] {row['variant_sequence']} [EOS]"
        ref_inputs = tokenizer(ref_seq, return_tensors="pt")
        var_inputs = tokenizer(var_seq, return_tensors="pt")
        with torch.no_grad():
            ref_outputs = model(**ref_inputs)
            var_outputs = model(**var_inputs)
            ref_logits = ref_outputs.logits[0, :-1]
            var_logits = var_outputs.logits[0, :-1]
            ref_tokens = ref_inputs['input_ids'][0, 1:]
            var_tokens = var_inputs['input_ids'][0, 1:]
            ref_score = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(ref_logits, ref_tokens, reduction='sum')
            var_score = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(var_logits, var_tokens, reduction='sum')
            score = (var_score - ref_score).item()
            scores.append(score)
    variants_df['score'] = scores
    return variants_df

variants = pd.DataFrame({
    'sequence': ['ATGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTA', 'ATGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTA'],
    'variant_sequence': ['ATGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTA', 'ATGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTA']
})

scored_variants = score_variants_hf(variants, gene='brca1', species='human', clade='primate')
print(scored_variants)
PY

The Hugging Face model code describes itself as a simplified demonstration wrapper, so scores from this route may not match the paper's model. The repository's src/scripts/score_sequences.py is the alternative, but the sources do not say where to get its checkpoint, tokeniser and embedding files.
The wrapper builds its configuration from the 'ctrl' configuration on the Hugging Face Hub, so loading needs that to be available.
The snippet does not pin a Hugging Face revision; this page was written from revision 397bbb87341c7afa569dd3139217fdbd10480d36.

notes: Worth a human look: the Hugging Face modeling_loleve.py says it is a simplified demonstration wrapper that builds a plain CTRLLMHeadModel, and it never mentions ESM embeddings or adaptive position embeddings, although the README and card list both. The model repository also holds gene_embeddings_v4.npz, which nothing in the HF code loads; example_usage.py uses the same wrapper. The README's clone URL (github.com/Marks-lab/LOL-EVE) and requirements file name differ from the actual repository (debbiemarkslab/LOL-EVE, requirement.txt), so the run guide uses the Hugging Face route. The existing source vep-uc-20261014-source-lol-eve is the same README at the same commit. Revision of 2026-11-27: the bioRxiv preprint v2 is now read. It confirms that the model it describes uses ESM2 gene embeddings, which the Hugging Face wrapper does not load. Its text layer has no IP address stamp; its first page carries the corresponding authors' email addresses, not copied to the page. Main-text pages are in two columns, so quotes from them are short single-column fragments. The structured parameters value is null: the paper gives 235 million for its model, and no saved file ties that count to the published Marks-lab/LOL-EVE weights.
